name: Torres del Paine
title: Holidays in Torres del Paine
intro: Granite towers, blue glaciers and pumas in Patagonia, near the end of the world. Here's what Torres del Paine is like with the family and when to go.
facts_note: Park tickets and campsites must be booked ahead. Check entry rules on GOV.UK before you book.
when_to_go: November to March is summer, with long days but strong winds. April brings autumn colours and fewer people. Winter is cold and quiet, but clear and still, and a good time to track pumas.

things.name: Grey Glacier boat
things.blurb: Sail up close to the face of a huge blue glacier.

things.name: Lago Pehoé catamaran
things.blurb: A boat across a turquoise lake below the Paine horns.

things.name: Mirador Cóndor
things.blurb: A short, steep climb to views of lakes and mountains, with condors overhead.

things.name: Base of the Towers
things.blurb: A full-day hike to the famous granite towers. For fit older children.

things.name: Puma tracking
things.blurb: Go out with a tracker for a chance to see a wild puma.

things.name: Horse riding
things.blurb: Ride across the steppe with local gauchos.

faqs.question: Is Patagonia good for a family holiday?
faqs.answer: Yes, for active families with children who enjoy walking. Lodges and boat trips make it doable without camping, and the scenery is jaw-dropping.

faqs.question: How many nights do you need?
faqs.answer: Four to six nights in the park, as part of a two or three week trip to Chile or Argentina.

faqs.question: Do UK families need a visa?
faqs.answer: No, British passport holders can visit Chile for a holiday without a visa. Check GOV.UK for the current rules.

faqs.question: How do you get there?
faqs.answer: Fly to Santiago, then on to Punta Arenas or Puerto Natales. The park is about two hours by road from Puerto Natales.
